title: Restriction of formal coherent modules is exact; exactness is local
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals; $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian], with exactness as in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. (1) For every open $U\subseteq X$, $U$ (with $\mathcal O_X|_U$) is a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I|_U\subseteq\mathcal O_U$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and the restriction $\rho_U:\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\to\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$, $(\mathcal F_n)\mapsto(\mathcal F_n|_U)$, $(\alpha_n)\mapsto(\alpha_n|_U)$, is a well-defined additive functor which is exact: it carries every short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ to a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$. (2) Let $X=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ be an open covering and $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal C$ morphisms of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ with $\alpha\circ\beta=0$. Then the sequence is exact at $\mathcal B$ if and only if for every $j$ the sequence $\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal A)\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal B)\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal C)$ is exact at $\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal B)$ in $\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})$; in particular $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ if and only if $0\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal A)\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal B)\to\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal C)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})$ for every $j$.

proof.text: (Restriction is defined.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be open. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, $U$ is locally Noetherian, and because $X$ is Noetherian its open subscheme $U$ is quasi-compact; hence $U$ is Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The restriction $\mathcal I|_U$ is a quasi-coherent ideal by restriction of quasi-coherent modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. For an object $(\mathcal F_n)$, each $\mathcal F_n|_U$ is coherent by locality of coherence [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover], and restriction carries $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n$ and the quotient maps to $(\mathcal I|_U)^n(\mathcal F_n|_U)$ and the corresponding quotient maps [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections]. Thus the restricted system satisfies the defining conditions of $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$, and restricting components defines a functor $\rho_U$; termwise addition makes it additive.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X, parts (2)--(3), with the restriction and coherence facts used in its proof

proof.text: (Restriction preserves kernels and cokernels.) Let $\alpha:(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ be a morphism. The cokernel is the termwise system $(\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n)_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]; restriction preserves these cokernels because they are colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. For the kernel use [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module-kernel]: the images $\mathcal K'_{l,m}=\operatorname{Im}(\ker\alpha_l\to\mathcal F_m)$ stabilize to $\mathcal K'_m$, and the quotients $\mathcal K'_m/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_m$ stabilize to the kernel levels $\mathcal K_n$, with the induced transition and structure maps. For every open $V\subseteq U$, the kernel sections are precisely $\ker(\alpha_l(V))$, so restricting a kernel sheaf gives the kernel of the restricted map. An image section is locally in the sectionwise image; the opens covering $V$ in $U$ are exactly the opens covering $V$ in $X$, so the same local description shows that image sheaves restrict to image sheaves. The subsheaf $\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_m$ is locally generated by sums of products of $n$ ideal sections and one module section; this description on opens inside $U$ is unchanged by restriction, hence its restriction equals $(\mathcal I|_U)^n(\mathcal K'_m|_U)$. Quotients restrict to quotients by the cited colimit-preservation lemma. Thus all the stabilized images, quotients, transition maps and maps to $\mathcal F_n$ restrict to their counterparts for $\alpha|_U$. The global stabilization bound is also a valid bound on $U$; if the construction on $U$ uses another bound, taking the larger one gives the same eventual systems via their transition isomorphisms. The cited kernel theorem on $U$ therefore identifies this restricted system and its structure morphism with a kernel of $\rho_U(\alpha)$.

proof.text: (Exactness of restriction.) In a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal A\xrightarrow\beta\mathcal B\xrightarrow\alpha\mathcal C\to0$, the first map exhibits $\mathcal A$ as the kernel of $\alpha$ and the second exhibits $\mathcal C$ as the cokernel of $\beta$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence, lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. Step 2 preserves both universal properties, so the restricted sequence is short exact. More generally the image is the kernel of the cokernel, hence is also preserved by Step 2; the equality of image and kernel characterizing exactness at a middle term is therefore preserved as well.

proof.text: (Exactness is local.) Let $X=\bigcup_jU_j$ and $\beta,\alpha$ be as in the statement. If the sequence is exact at $\mathcal B$, Step 3 gives exactness after every restriction. Conversely, let $\mathcal K=\ker\alpha$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. The equation $\alpha\beta=0$ gives a unique factorization $\beta=\iota\gamma$ through the kernel inclusion $\iota:\mathcal K\to\mathcal B$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. On each $U_j$, local exactness says that $\rho_{U_j}(\gamma)$ is an epimorphism, because exactness at $\rho_{U_j}(\mathcal B)$ is equivalent to the map into its kernel being epi in an abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift]. Hence the induced map from the cokernel $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{Coker}\gamma$ restricts to zero on every $U_j$. Its components are sheaf morphisms whose restrictions are zero, so every component of $\mathcal Q$ is zero; the locality of formal-module isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-isomorphism-local] then gives $\mathcal Q=0$. Thus $\gamma$ is epi and the original sequence is exact at $\mathcal B$ by the same abelian criterion.

proof.text: (Short exact sequences.) Apply the preceding equivalence to the three-term complex $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\to0$. Exactness at the two end terms is the monomorphism and epimorphism clauses of a short exact sequence, and restriction preserves those by Step 2. Therefore the global sequence is short exact exactly when every restricted sequence is short exact.
